name: Harlow

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: mandatory licensing applies to HMOs with five or more people from two or more households. A town-wide Article 4 direction means converting a home to an HMO needs full planning permission, and some council-built homes carry covenants limiting them to single-family use.
licensing.fee: £850 (or £600 for accredited landlords) for a mandatory HMO licence of up to six bedrooms; licences last one year, renewal £350 (£225)

housing: Harlow is a post-war new town in west Essex, laid out in neighbourhoods of terraced houses, maisonettes and low-rise flats around local shopping centres, with a high share of social housing. Many former council homes are now privately let, and office blocks in and near the town centre have been converted into flats. Newer estates at Church Langley and Newhall add family houses, and Old Harlow keeps its historic village core. Private renting grew quickly between 2011 and 2021, helped by commuting to London and Cambridge.
checkinTips: New town terraces and maisonettes: record flat roofs, communal walkways, stairwells, garages in separate blocks and the key or fob count for each.
Office blocks converted into flats near the town centre: note the size of each room, ventilation, fire doors and alarms, and any condensation.
Former council houses now privately let: photograph the boiler, windows, external doors and the condition of gardens and fencing.
Shared homes: an HMO needs planning permission under the town-wide Article 4 direction, so check the licence and photograph each room's lock and furniture.
Newer homes at Newhall and Church Langley: note snagging still outstanding, meter readings and parking allocations.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Harlow Council's environmental health (private sector housing) team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
